title: Placement prioritizer and soft-drain playbook for multi-zone dedicated fleets
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a placement prioritizer and a controlled soft-drain / graceful evacuation playbook for regional and multi-zone Dedicated fleets that enforces throughput contracts, respects per-tenant jurisdictional tags, and allows predictable autoscaling and failover with minimal client-visible disruption.

Scope:
- New placement prioritizer service that scores candidate pools by: jurisdictional tag match, tenant reservation eligibility, warmness score (prewarmed KV cache / model hot state), latency headroom, and current throughput utilization.
- Soft-drain strategy: staged concurrency decrement (k-rate), preferential eviction of non-reserved lanes, and session-aware shift for long-running prompts.
- Failover routing: prioritized pool list per-tenant that preserves data-boundary constraints; optional automatic spill-to-replica policy when no local capacity available.
- Autoscaler hooks: allow autoscaler to use prioritizer signals and to perform scale-down windows aligned to soft-drain stages.

Success criteria / acceptance:
- 99.95% of requests for reserved-tenants continue to meet latency SLO during single-zone evacuation (measured over 15 min windows).
- Controlled soft-drain produces <1% increase in 99th percentile latency for reserved lanes during 10k QPS simulated drain tests.
- Placement decisions match residency constraints (jurisdiction tags) 100% of the time; violations are logged and blocked.
- Rollout plan validated via canary on two internal tenants and no customer incident during dry-run.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: UI work in Console (separate PM ticket), long-term cross-region DR choreography (separate epic).
comments: 2026-02-16 Maya Chen: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to prototype prioritizer as a standalone scoring service with a feature flag. Initial scoring factors listed and weight defaults assigned (jurisdiction=1.0, reservation=1.2, warmness=0.8, latency_headroom=0.9, utilization_penalty=0.7).
2026-02-20 Liam O'Connor: Implemented initial scorer and unit tests. Local simulation shows prioritizer reduces cross-jurisdiction placements to zero in deterministic inputs. Draft PR opened: #142.

2026-02-25 Engineering Review (Arch): Concern about contention between autoscaler and soft-drain. Decision: autoscaler will expose a gentle-scale-down request with suggested drain window; prioritizer will return a drain-score that autoscaler consumes. Follow-up: define control loop stability constraints.
2026-02-27 Sofia Patel (Product): PM feedback: Need explicit operator mode for legal teams to pin hard-blocks on spillover for specific tenants. Added requirement: operator-block list with audit log.

2026-03-01 Jon Rivera (SRE): Ran simulated single-zone evacuation with 10k QPS; observed 0.8% increase in p99 for reserved lanes, 3.6% for best-effort lanes. Suggest tuning k-rate from 5%/sec to 2%/sec and increase warm-prewarming threshold.

2026-03-03 Liam O'Connor: Updated soft-drain strategy: introduce tiered-k-rate (reserved lanes decay slower), and session-anchoring for in-progress long requests. Benchmarks re-run show reserved lanes p99 delta reduced to 0.4%.

2026-03-05 Maya Chen: Security review kickoff scheduled. Confirmed we must integrate KMS audit context into placement logs for regulatory tenants. Marked security_review_required=true. Next steps: finalize canary plan and run two dry-run evacuations on staging.
implementation_notes: Scorer will be a small Go service behind a k8s service. Weighting config stored in ConfigStore and exposed via runtime feature flag. Soft-drain orchestrator will be part of fleet-manager with an API: /drain/start -> accepts drain-window, lane-priority, hard-block-list. Autoscaler changes: expose gentle-scale-down endpoint that accepts suggested drain-plan. Ensure metrics: drain-progress, residual-capacity, tenant-violations.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for scoring function with synthetic tag matrices. 2) Chaos sim: single-zone evacuation with 0/25/50/75/100% reserved load mixes. 3) Integration: canary warmup on two internal tenants and a scheduled dry-run on staging. 4) Regression: ensure no regressions in placement latency (<5ms median extra).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy autoscaler interactions causing oscillation. Mitigation: conservative cooldowns and require drain-plan handshake before scale-down. Risk: operator misconfig leads to over-blocking. Mitigation: preview dry-run mode + audit logs and reversible operator flags. Risk: misclassification of tenant tags. Mitigation: strict validation and reject placements that would violate hard-blocks.
followups: PM-8342: Console UX for lane reservations and operator blocks
